Mapped OSM roofs and broad building faces are traversable. Rivers slow your pace. Hold a direction and sprint for county travel; slow down to explore. Wall runs have a finite lift budget and expire after 1.6 seconds. Land or leave the wall to recharge.

The county is drawn at true scale: 1 unit is 1 metre, 38.6 × 57.2 km. Buildings, roads, rivers and the Route 66 alignment come from an offline OpenStreetMap snapshot; terrain height and trees are procedural. The 2,753-footprint count measures mapped OSM data, not every real building. Only the explorer is out of scale: 26 m/s run, 68 m/s sprint (152 mph), a 6.4 m leap. Crossing the county on foot takes about 14 minutes, so warp with 1–6 or click the map. Comfort mode disables camera roll and speed-FOV effects.
